It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world where political powers grow cold toward the Gospel and seek to silence His messengers, and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the mandate of public witness when the law of the land forbids it? [13, 252, 1361, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who “do not spare the flock” or use the law as a “scourge” against the faithful, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion” against the King? [13, 20, 1150, 1361, 1390, 1425, 1471, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many seek “diplomatic relations” with a “distinctively anti-Christian agenda” to avoid the “scars” of the cross, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Master personally governs the “record of history” by reminding us that our “citizenship is in heaven” [11, 15, 28, 788, 1183, 1316, 1391, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John Calvin** and **John MacArthur**—teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the state’s attempt to criminalize your witness is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones when they have served His administration” [15, 68, 812, 1143, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Mandate to Proclaim Despite the Sword**

**Verse**
“But Peter and the other apostles answered and said: ‘We ought to obey God rather than men. The God of our fathers raised up Jesus whom you murdered by hanging on a tree. Him God has exalted to His right hand to be Prince and Savior, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins’ ” (Acts 5:29–31). [48, 914, 1070, 1130, 1176, 1230, 1247, 1249, 1256, 1300, 1431, 1529, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture reveals that the church has a “binding and authoritative mandate” from the Savior that no earthly “legislative body” can cancel or control [11, 15, 785, 1316, 1503, 1720, Conversation History]. While we are commanded to “render therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s,” the Reformed tradition asserts that “Jesus Christ alone is the head of the church,” and we must “refuse to yield submission” to any ruler who tries to “tamper with or attempt to tone down the gospel” (Matthew 22:21; Colossians 1:18; Galatians 2:5) [19, 131, 1104, 1105, 1144, 1155, 1316, 1500, 1528, 1529, 1545, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. The “record of history” shows that though the “body of the believer” may be “incarcerated,” the “word of God is not chained,” and its “decisions are immutable” (2 Timothy 2:9) [11, 25, 41, 123, 1268, 1283, 1314, 1420, 1504, 1646, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “political maneuvering and lobbying” when the truth is at stake; instead, “be bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much conflict” (1 Thessalonians 2:2) [51, 53, 76, 91, 123, 1073, 1406, 1461, 1503, 1670, Conversation History]. Remember that “your life is not your own” because “you were bought at a price,” and your “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God” even if the “nations rage” (1 Corinthians 6:20; Titus 2:10; Psalm 2:1) [11, 12, 21, 101, 212, 265, 361, 772, 932, 988, 1132, 1138, 1242, 1262, 1406, 1503, 1515, 1572, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Jurisdiction**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “religious leaders” were “punctilious” about “legal minutiae,” yet they “neglected the weightier matters” of “justice and mercy,” often using “religious courts” to silence the truth (Matthew 23:23) [8, 176, 177, 205, 1091, 1260, 1333, 1720, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our standing, showing that Christ’s rule is “mediated... solely and only by His revealed truth,” and the “church militant” is an “assembly of the citizens of heaven” who do not use “carnal weaponry” to expand His kingdom (John 18:36; Philippians 3:20; 2 Corinthians 10:4) [13, 19, 21, 26, 29, 32, 53, 92, 142, 1081, 1113, 1183, 1313, 1422, 1426, 1473, 1529, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Christian Posture Toward Hostile Rulers**

**Verse**
“Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist are appointed by God. Therefore whoever resists the authority resists the ordinance of God, and those who resist will bring judgment on themselves... For he is God’s minister to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is God’s minister, an avenger to execute wrath on him who practices evil” (Romans 13:1–4). [925, 981, 1105, 1110, 1224, 1246, 1261, 1284, 1342, 1422, 1473, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture handles “unreasonable” authorities by commanding the saint to “be submissive to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the harsh” (1 Peter 2:18) [298, 927, 983, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition teaches that the state is “appointed by God” to maintain “civil peace” and “retard the corruption” of a fallen world, but this authority is “secondary” to the King who “sovereignly orders everything He has made” [15, 18, 76, 78, 318, 765, 812, 1110, 1143, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. When a ruler “despises authority” or “blasphemes the name of the LORD,” he acts as a “usurper” and a “spiritual swindler” who must ultimately answer to the “Lord, the righteous Judge” (2 Peter 2:10; 2 Timothy 4:8) [1, 236, 267, 313, 351, 881, 950, 958, 1058, 1059, 1251, 1344, 1407, 1506, 1529, 1572, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “worldly philosophy” that suggests your primary battle is political; instead, you must “discipline your mind” to “honor all people. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the king” (1 Peter 2:17) [15, 39, 47, 68, 76, 91, 116, 926, 982, 1106, 1143, 1181, 1202, 1214, 1406, 1502, 1532, 1670, 1709, Conversation History]. “Trade in your worry for trust,” knowing that “the Lord has established His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all,” and He will “respond to the prayer of the destitute” (Psalm 103:19; 102:17) [11, 15, 24, 68, 88, 94, 201, 318, 1033, 1143, 1408, 1515, 1532, 1572, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Theocracy vs. Pilgrimage**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “national greatness” and “large and beautiful cities” were often seen as “temporal signs” of God’s favor [409, 620, 627, 934, 950, 1083, 1122, 1172, 1313, 1342, 1353, 1519, 1546, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our view, revealing that we are “sojourners and pilgrims” whose “citizenship is in heaven,” making the “burial of a donkey” or the loss of an earthly building irrelevant to our standing as “joint heirs with Christ” (1 Peter 2:11; Philippians 3:20; Romans 8:17) [13, 14, 21, 26, 28, 38, 142, 248, 440, 1023, 1029, 1030, 1032, 1088, 1132, 1135, 1159, 1167, 1177, 1183, 1203, 1210, 1236, 1259, 1313, 1320, 1326, 1342, 1426, 1529, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: Suffering for the Witness of the King**

**Verse**
“ ‘Remember the word that I said to you, “A servant is not greater than his master.” If they persecuted Me, they will also persecute you. If they kept My word, they will keep yours also. But all these things they will do to you for My name’s sake, because they do not know Him who sent Me’ ” (John 15:20–21). [53, 893, 942, 1056, 1316, 1513, 1596, 1672, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Charles Spurgeon**—notes that “it is in the very order of things” that the “spotless purity of truth” will be at war with the “blackness of heresy and lies” [1359, 1391, Conversation History]. Persecution and criminalization are the “theatre” where God displays His “matchless grace,” using the “scars” of His “messengers” to “testify to the gospel of the grace of God” (Acts 20:24) [47, 323, 782, 843, 861, 892, 934, 975, 1022, Conversation History]. The “record of history” is filled with “valiant warriors for the truth,” such as Sanctus, who replied to every accusation by saying, “ ‘I am a Christian,’ ” and Polycarp, who refused to curse Christ despite being “burned alive on the spot” [248, 249, 1365, 1367, 1614, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “all who desire to live godly in Christ Jesus will suffer persecution,” yet they are “protected by the power of God” (2 Timothy 3:12; 1 Peter 1:5) [13, 24, 60, 74, 101, 142, 192, 201, 237, 313, 385, 442, 473, 830, 893, 1012, 1016, 1018, 1026, 1030, 1132, 1143, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1426, 1450, 1515, 1646, 1670, 1684, Conversation History]. You should find “tranquility of soul” by resting on the “surest foundation,” knowing that “death is but a harmless shadow for the sheep of the Good Shepherd” (2 Timothy 2:19; Psalm 23:4) [11, 24, 31, 147, 176, 198, 211, 222, 273, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 359, 361, 405, 413, 414, 442, 444, 449, 591, 718, 836, 844, 856, 881, 883, 1016, 1032, 1033, 1138, 1143, 1221, 1313, 1407, 1426, 1441, 1445, 1447, 1450, 1515, 1646, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual vs. Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “animal sacrifices” were a “shadow” of the coming Redeemer, and “testifying in a dispute” required strict “safeguards” to establish “justice for all” (Deuteronomy 17:6) [11, 330, 333, 367, 402, 1012, 1069, 1072, 1112, 1133, 1185, 1230, 1288, 1289, 1294, 1313, 1317, 1332, 1340, 1344, 1346, 1365, 1430, 1442, 1473, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” showing that the “church militant” conquers not through “carnal weaponry” but “by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony,” for the “Holy Spirit temple” is the body of the believer (Revelation 12:11; 1 Corinthians 6:19) [11, 12, 13, 21, 32, 92, 101, 186, 238, 240, 264, 833, 837, 937, 1054, 1059, 1083, 1093, 1113, 1114, 1117, 1118, 1119, 1120, 1138, 1158, 1202, 1208, 1210, 1219, 1220, 1243, 1262, 1267, 1313, 1315, 1402, 1403, 1406, 1417, 1426, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Final Triumph and the King’s Return**

**Verse**
“Then the seventh angel sounded: And there were loud voices in heaven, saying, ‘The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever!’ ” (Revelation 11:15). [103, 133, 158, 174, 650, 1199, 1315, 1524, 1636, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “noise and tumult” of “troublesome times” by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 21, 23, 24, 31, 103, 136, 815, 1199, 1300, 1311, 1315, 1503, 1515, 1524, 1532, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. On that Day, the “Lord Savior” will “judge between the nations,” and every human “monument of pride” or “storage city” will “vanish—like smoke they vanish away” (Isaiah 2:4; Psalm 102:3) [11, 32, 35, 37, 43, 63, 210, 452, 470, 789, 818, 825, 827, 855, 867, 869, 903, 912, 917, 940, 947, 952, 958, 976, 1004, 1113, 1233, 1259, 1260, 1266, 1268, 1288, 1290, 1300, 1301, 1315, 1402, 1460, 1473, 1519, 1684, 1720, Conversation History]. The “church triumphant” will find “perfect justice” and God will “wipe away every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4) [13, 14, 21, 24, 32, 92, 94, 109, 121, 152, 171, 174, 188, 190, 201, 224, 301, 321, 331, 333, 334, 337, 339, 352, 412, 459, 470, 719, 730, 816, 822, 852, 903, 943, 948, 1009, 1020, 1033, 1039, 1128, 1132, 1143, 1162, 1197, 1203, 1206, 1211, 1218, 1243, 1252, 1255, 1257, 1259, 1282, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1426, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” resting upon the “surest foundation,” for if God has “magnified Your word above all Your name,” His “everlasting dominion” is “secure” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; Psalm 138:2; Daniel 7:14) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 176, 201, 266, 273, 278, 313, 352, 386, 412, 602, 614, 630, 788, 869, 921, 958, 1035, 1132, 1143, 1183, 1300, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1315, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. You can find “tranquility of soul” by looking past your “momentary, light affliction,” knowing that “He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ” (Philippians 1:6; 2 Corinthians 4:17) [5, 14, 21, 113, 152, 192, 201, 304, 313, 315, 352, 829, 901, 920, 1021, 1072, 1101, 1132, 1143, 1408, 1515, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 291, 297, 300, 311, 324, 325, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 424, 444, 449, 591, 834, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

Based on this verse, continuationists ask, if New Testament prophecy was infallible like Old Testament prophecy, then why did Paul tell the Thessalonians to test it carefully, or to examine it carefully? Well, we would respond with the following observations. First of all, I think it's important to note that Paul's statement "Do not despise prophetic utterances" was written at a time when everyone agrees that the gift of prophecy was still active. So when cessationists reject the false predictions being made by self-appointed modern prophets, they're not disobeying Paul's command, rather they're taking the command to test things seriously. When we test modern prophets using the biblical standards, we are right then to reject those who do not pass the test.

In the words of the apostle Paul, “They being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and seeking to establish their own righteousness, [did not submit] to the righteousness of God” (Rom. 10:3). This particular legalist was desperate to make himself look good in others’ eyes, regardless of what God thought of him. So instead of asking the question Jesus’ reply ought to have prompted from him, he asked, “Who is my neighbor?” (Luke 10:29). Notice, first of all, that he skipped right over the part about loving God with all his heart, soul, mind, and strength. Instead, he wants to discuss a technical point about the identity of one’s neighbor. Because, as Jesus says elsewhere, the traditional rabbinical and popular interpretation of Leviticus 19:18 (“Love your neighbor as yourself”) is “You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy” (Matt. 5:43). That takes all the force out of the command, because if you’re free to hate your enemy, then you’re relieved from the duty of loving anyone whom you decide to regard as an enemy. Under that interpretation, you have no legal or moral obligation to love anyone you don’t really want to.

Some Context for This Parable At this point in Luke’s narrative (16:16–18), Jesus sums up in a few words everything He ever preached about the Pharisees, the law, the gospel, and true righteousness. He does so by making three quick points. One, the old covenant is giving way to the new. “The law and the prophets were until John. Since that time the kingdom of God has been preached, and everyone is pressing into it” (v. 16). The threats and punishments of the law were being answered by the promises of the gospel and the sacrifice of Christ. So the way was wide open for sinners to enter the kingdom, and they were already pressing in. But for those arrogant enough to insist on measuring their own performance by the law, the case remained hopeless. Although they thought they were sufficiently righteous, they would find themselves condemned forever.

Today, however, the threats are much more subtle, primarily because the contemporary evangelical movement has lost its interest in doctrine. The current of mainstream evangelicalism is driven by pragmatic concerns, not theological ones. Church growth gurus worry about what draws a crowd, not about what the Bible says. Because it successfully appeals to unredeemed flesh, prosperity preachers make man the master, as if Christ were some sort of genie in a bottle—obliged to grant health, wealth, and happiness to those who send enough money. Even within some conservative circles, pragmatic worldly methods (including crass humor and coarse speech) and almost boundless adaptations of the worst of worldly music are aggressively defended as long as they get visible results. The sad reality is that popularity, not faithfulness to Christ and His Word, has become evangelicalism’s new standard of measure and its current brand of no-lordship ideology.

To the Colossians, Paul would similarly underscore the all-encompassing implications of Christ’s sovereign lordship: “Whatever you do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus” (Col. 3:17), even telling the slaves in that congregation, “Whatever you do, do your work heartily, as for the Lord” (v. 23). Over and over again, perhaps more than any other theme, Paul’s writings evidence an intimate understanding of the subservient relationship of a believer to Christ—namely, that Jesus is his Master and he is but a slave.

As Paul explained to Timothy: The firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, “The Lord knows those who are His,” and, “Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness.” Now in a large house there are not only gold and silver vessels, but also vessels of wood and of earthenware, and some to honor and some to dishonor. Therefore, if anyone cleanses himself from these things, he will be a vessel for honor, sanctified, useful to the Master, prepared for every good work. Now flee from youthful lusts and pursue righteousness, faith, love and peace, with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart. (2 Tim. 2:19–22)

He is both our Lord and our God. He is the King over every individual believer, over His entire church, and over every created thing. Though unbelievers reject His authority in this life, there will come a day when “EVERY KNEE WILL BOW” and “every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord” (Phil. 2:10–11). Enter into the joy of your Master.”

The gospel, proclaimed in its fullness, necessarily includes the lordship of Jesus Christ. As Paul would tell the Romans, “If you confess with your mouth Jesus as Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved” (Rom. 10:9, emphasis added). When asked, “What must I do to be saved?” he similarly instructed the Philippian jailer, “Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved” (Acts 16:31, emphasis added). In explaining the gospel to the Jews on the day of Pentecost, Peter ended his sermon with these words: “Therefore let all the house of Israel know for certain that God has made Him both Lord and Christ—this Jesus whom you crucified” (Acts 2:36, emphasis added).
